sample.name: Julia B. Tuttle's Homestead
facts: Tuttle bought 644 acres on the north bank of the Miami River, including Fort Dallas.
Her home was a two-story stone building, built in 1849 as Fort Dallas officers' quarters.
A marker for Tuttle was erected in 2020 by Miami-Dade County at Fort Dallas Park.

sample.name: Dr. Luis Henry Debayle
facts: The bust in Collins Park was presented to Miami Beach by the city of Leon, Nicaragua, in 1959.

sample.name: Alhambra Water Tower
facts: Designed by H. George Fink and Denman Fink to look like a lighthouse.
Built in 1924, it conceals a steel water tank inside reinforced concrete.
Part of the city water supply until 1931, then abandoned.

sample.name: Dade County War Memorial
facts: Sculpted by Edward Codere and dedicated in Bayfront Park in 1943.
Depression Moderne structure topped by an eagle, listing Dade County World War II dead.
A 1990s update added the names of more than 500 Dade Countians.

sample.name: Flagler Memorial Monument
facts: A 110-foot obelisk honoring Henry Flagler, who died in 1913.
Four 18-foot statues at its base represent education, industry, prosperity and pioneering spirit.
Commissioned by Carl Fisher and designed by sculptor H.P. Peterson.

sample.name: Julia Sturtevant Tuttle
facts: The 10-foot bronze statue shows Tuttle holding oranges and blossoms.
Scenes from Miami's 1896 incorporation are engraved on the statue's skirt.
Unveiled July 28, 2010, by the Miami-Dade County Commission for Women and partners.

sample.name: The Liberty Column
facts: Memorial column in Bayfront Park in downtown Miami.

sample.name: Julia Deforest Tuttle
facts: Julia Tuttle is buried in the Miami City Cemetery.
Tuttle is the only woman to found a major U.S. city.

sample.name: Brickell Mausoleum
facts: Built in 1924, it is the only surviving structure associated with the Brickell family.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places on January 4, 1989.
Stands in Mary Brickell Park at 501 Brickell Avenue.

sample.name: Calle Ocho Walk of Fame
facts: Initiated in 1987 to honor Latin figures in entertainment, arts and public life.

sample.name: Iron Arrow Mound
facts: Iron Arrow was founded in November 1926 by first University of Miami president Bowman Foster Ashe.
The society is based on the ideals and traditions of the Seminole Indian Nation.
Inductees keep a 24-hour drum vigil and tend fires on the mound.

sample.name: Our Heroes
facts: The Confederate monument was erected in 1913 by the South Cross Chapter, United Daughters of the Confederacy.
It first stood outside the old Dade County Courthouse before moving to Miami City Cemetery.
Inscription: “United Daughters of the Confederacy”

sample.name: The Bahama Dingy
facts: Displays a Bahama dinghy donated by Bill Munroe, grandson of Commodore Ralph Munroe.
Historical marker stands about 200 yards west of the Cape Florida Lighthouse.

sample.name: Claude D. Pepper
facts: Monument to Claude D. Pepper in Bayfront Park, downtown Miami.
Pepper served Florida in the U.S. Senate 1936-1951 and the U.S. House 1963-1989.

sample.name: George Fink’s Studio
facts: Built in 1925 as the office of architect H. George Fink, a cousin of founder George Merrick.
Many early Coral Gables homes were designed here starting in 1925.
Address: 2506 Ponce de Leon Boulevard, Coral Gables

sample.name: Lincoln-Drexel Building
facts: 2 stories tall

sample.name: Simon Bolivar
facts: The bronze statue was a gift from the government of Venezuela, dedicated in 1984.
It stands a little over 8 feet high at Bayfront Park.

sample.name: South Pointe Park Lighthouse
facts: An art piece called Obstinate Lighthouse by German artist Tobias Rehberger.
Completed in 2011 as part of the city's Art in Public Places program.
The 55-foot tower has 16 staggered sections of aluminum, frosted glass and LED lights.

sample.name: Jose Marti Memorial
facts: A plaque marks the 100th anniversary of Jose Marti's death in 1995, donated by the Knights of Columbus.
The park also has a map of Cuba with a quote from Marti.

sample.name: Carlos J. Finlay
facts: The bust was sculpted by Ravenet in 1948 and dedicated in Collins Park on August 20, 1949.
The bust was presented to Miami Beach by the Republic of Cuba.
Finlay was a Cuban physician who found that mosquitoes transmit yellow fever.

sample.name: Queen Miami Beach
facts: The restaurant occupies a theater building at 550 Washington Avenue designed by Henry Hohauser.
Dates from 1935
Designed by Henry Hohauser

sample.name: General Antonio Macro memorial
facts: The bust of Antonio Maceo by sculptor Tony Lopez stands at SW 13th Avenue and SW 8th Street.
It is described as the first Maceo monument in a public park in the United States.
Maceo (1845-1896) was second in command of the Cuban Army of Independence.

sample.name: Simon Bolivar
facts: A historical marker at the monument was erected in 1997 by the Comite Pro Busto Simon Bolivar.
Miami Beach holds an annual Simon Bolivar y Las Americas Day ceremony at the monument in Collins Park.

sample.name: Section of the Berlin Wall
facts: The segment is 12 feet tall, 3 feet wide and weighs four and a half tons.
Unveiled on November 9, 2014, at Miami Dade College's downtown campus.

sample.name: Venetian Way
facts: The causeway follows the route of the Collins Bridge, a wooden bridge built in 1913.
The Venetian Causeway was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1989.
The causeway is 2.8 miles long and has two bascule bridges.
